dossier.public_summary: The four transits seen in TESS have very different depths, with one almost undetectable, so the signal is not steady. There is also a 2.1x difference between odd and even transits and the 3-hour transit is too long for this small M-dwarf star. Together this favours an eclipsing binary or a few spurious dips over a planet.

reasons.why: depths are inconsistent: first transit 1084 ppm sigma -4.4 while mean 8452 ppm, second 12095 ppm sigma +2.3, third 11521 ppm sigma +1.9, fourth 11286 ppm sigma +1.8. chi2 44.545 dof 3, share_of_top_3 0.997, with only first 4 transits and p_chance 0.02242 a few bad transits explain the signal.

odd-even depth difference 0.5154 (7401 ppm: odd 14360 ppm, even 6958 ppm, ratio 2.1) drives xgboost planet_rank 0.09; sector_oe_max_sigma 3.327 in 1 sector over 3 and sector_oe_same_sign_share 1 favours a binary at twice the period.

observed 3 h vs central 1.964 h ratio 1.527 with fit_log_density_ratio -0.8596 and star_density_penalty 44.17 share 0.364 shows duration too long for the 0.3211 Rsun M dwarf, inconsistent with a central planet transit.
flat bottom does not outweigh the inconsistent depths and density mismatch; flat bottom alone does not make a planet when other checks point to binary/bad data.
